changes.change: Added an explicit 'Compilation scope boundary' paragraph: compile only the rules necessary to reproduce the 109 approved scenarios and their governing structural context; any domain-ruleset band/threshold recorded as unset (e.g. marked '[U]') must be excluded from compilation and recorded as a follow-on item, never estimated.
changes.reason: User-identified gap during post-hardening review: STOP condition 1 (section 12) is scoped to 'any of the 109 scenarios' and would not obviously fire for a domain-ruleset table row with an unset threshold that no approved scenario exercises (concrete example found: haematology ruleset HAEM-U-D-5, 'marked leucocytosis with abnormal differential pattern', recorded as '[U] -- threshold not set' inside an otherwise-governed within-days urgency table). The prior general prohibition ('do not invent a new clinical rule') and the fail-closed compiler requirement already existed but did not explicitly name this failure mode. A proactive scope-bounding instruction was chosen over a 16th STOP condition because: (1) it prevents the ambiguity rather than reacting to it; (2) an unset '[U]' threshold is an already-known, already-classified authoring gap, not a novel discovery requiring escalation, so a STOP is the wrong severity; (3) this pattern recurs across multiple domains (e.g. iron/inflammatory IRIN-U2/IRIN-U3, thyroid THY-U2), so a STOP condition would trigger repeatedly for a uniformly-already-decided disposition rather than being handled once by a scoping rule.
changes.classification: Scope-narrowing safety correction. Reduces risk (closes an ambiguity that could permit undetected clinical-rule invention); does not expand scope, does not touch clinical content, does not change front matter, does not require re-running Stage 2A/2B verification against new authority files.
